The case

Serious energy, explained like a human.

The world needs abundant low-carbon electricity that works in every season, at every hour. Nuclear is not the only answer—but any credible path to climate stability and energy security should understand what it can do.

Evidence snapshot

Start with what we can measure.

These figures begin the conversation. Every claim should lead back to a transparent, reputable source.

Median grams of CO₂-equivalent per kilowatt-hour—comparable with wind and far below fossil generation.

Common claims

Less fear. More perspective.

Nuclear deserves the same standard we should demand of every energy source: complete evidence, meaningful context and honest trade-offs.

Waste

“The waste has no solution.”

Used fuel is compact, contained and carefully tracked. Deep geological disposal is a technically mature long-term solution, and some fuel can be recycled.

Safety

“Nuclear is uniquely dangerous.”

Major accidents matter. So do routine deaths and pollution from other sources. Fair comparisons measure harm per unit of energy produced.

The grid

“Renewables make it unnecessary.”

Wind, solar, storage, grids and nuclear solve different parts of the same system. The practical question is which mix delivers clean, reliable power.

Delivery

“It always takes too long.”

Some projects run late; others are delivered repeatedly and efficiently. Policy stability, standardisation and construction capability shape outcomes.

Editorial standard

Warm in tone. Rigorous in method.

✦

Primary sources first

Prefer regulators, system operators, peer-reviewed research and original datasets.

◌

Context over slogans

Numbers should include units, assumptions, timescales and a fair comparator.

☼

Uncertainty stated

Show what is known, what is contested and what remains uncertain.

⌁

Corrections welcomed

Credibility means changing the record openly when better evidence appears.
